div.div: The evaluator reports how close a candidate came to failing: binding ratio = largest measured / limit; below 1 passes, promotion needs at most 0.9 [I1]

CANDIDATE
candidates/<id>/
one idea, parent-linked, never modified (B5)

VERIFY
frozen tree hash = manifest?
if not: refuse to evaluate
(human-owned, versioned)

VISIBLE set
20 seeds [I3] x 5 s [I4]; agents may read it
HELD-OUT a: 3 cores, perception 40 Hz [I6]; 8 seeds [I5]
HELD-OUT b: another robot, 200 ms GPU grasp planner [I7], no DLA; 8 seeds [I5]

GATE, per input set (limit -> ratio)
- every chain instance due completes
- hard chains: 0 deadline misses; worst e2e / deadline
- soft chains: misses <= 5 % [I8]; p99 e2e / deadline, miss ratio / limit
- mean decision time < 2 ms [I9]; time / limit
- order probe: reversed seeds give identical results
- only ready jobs, allowed resources

BINDING RATIO
= the LARGEST measured / limit over every check and every input set
(also called the margin)

VERDICT
ACCEPTED: all checks pass (binding below 1)
REJECTED: a check fails
INVALID: cannot count by design (e.g. a quick development run)
promotable only if binding <= 0.9 [I1]

INTEGRITY CHECKS (each closes one way a fast result can be fake): model ran exactly once per call (no skipping or caching) | fixed noise consumed exactly once | output came from the device (no silent host fall-back) | order probe (no carried state) | provenance hashes of every file read | candidate tree hash before = after the run

BINDING RATIOS OF THE DEMONSTRATION RUN on one scale (illustrative output of the local scheduling simulator, not a real platform). Bars are to scale; zones are set by the margin cap and the pass limit.
baseline (calibration) [I10]: 0.49 accepted [calc]
EDF, same placement [I11]: 0.6 accepted [calc]
R1 earliest-finish placement [I12]: 0.434 accepted
R1 + perception-first dispatch [I13]: 0.474 promoted
R1 earliest-finish + reservation [I14]: 0.78 accepted, not promotable
R1 baseline placement + reservation [I15]: 0.807 accepted, not promotable

0.85 [I2]
first-campaign cap

0.9 [I1]
cap here

1.0 = a limit reached
-> REJECTED
promotable zone (if the range rule also holds, diagram 04)

WHY A MARGIN AND NOT JUST A PASS
A pass close to 1 means the next small change breaks it, or the candidate exploits the edge of a limit: such a run is 'accepted, low margin' and never promoted.
Limits come from legitimate runs (B1), not a guess: a limit tighter than legitimate noise rejects correct work.

Legend: amber = the frozen judge | blue = inputs agents may read / candidate files | pale red = held-out inputs agents never read | chart: bar = binding ratio (green, thick = promoted); purple dashed = first-campaign cap; amber = cap in the scheduling topic; red = pass limit 1.0

Sources. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown. [Pn] = public (cited paper, or my arithmetic on public mathematics); [In] = illustrative (a design parameter of the harness, a round value that keeps the shape of the first campaign, or output of the demonstration scheduling simulator; never a measurement of a real platform); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/B2-the-frozen-evaluator.md (frozen = human-owned, hash-pinned, versioned; four jobs; integrity table; verdicts); notes/C2-the-scheduling-topic.md (gate per input set, binding definition, held-out workloads); notes/C3-calibration.md (calibration and round-1 table). [calc]: baseline binding = max(visible 0.49, a 0.34, b 0.44); EDF binding = max(visible 0.6, a 0.26, b 0.43). The R1 rows use each record's single 'binding' value.
[I1] harness_margin_cap_scheduling = 0.9 binding ratio. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
[I2] harness_margin_cap_first_campaign = 0.85 binding ratio. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
[I3] topic_visible_seeds = 20 seeds. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
[I4] topic_horizon_s = 5 s. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
[I5] topic_heldout_seeds = 8 seeds per held-out workload. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
[I6] sched_heldout_a = {cpu_cores 3, perception_hz 40} -. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
[I7] sched_heldout_b_grasp_ms = 200 ms. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
[I8] topic_soft_miss_limit = 5 %. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
[I9] topic_decision_time_limit_ms = 2 ms. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
[I10] sched_baseline = {median 34.7, min 32.3, max 45.4, binding_visible 0.49, binding_a 0.34, binding_b 0.44} ms / binding. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
[I11] sched_edf_gpu_first = {median 34.5, min 31.6, max 41.6, binding_visible 0.6, binding_a 0.26, binding_b 0.43} ms / binding. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
[I12] sched_r1_eft_placement = {median 27.8, min 23.7, max 34.2, binding 0.434} ms / binding. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
[I13] sched_r1_eft_metric_first = {median 25.8, min 23.7, max 30.7, binding 0.474} ms / binding. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
[I14] sched_r1_eft_reserve = {median 23.9, min 23.7, max 24.1, binding 0.78} ms / binding. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
[I15] sched_r1_metric_reserve = {median 30, min 27.9, max 31.2, binding 0.807} ms / binding. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
